quest.title: Miraculous Crown
quest.description: The end of the fantastical adventure approaches. At its final destination, will Madame Zuria's child get better, as you all hope?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Thelxie's Badge x15, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Thelxie's Fantastic Adventures x1

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Freminet! Thelxie! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: #Hello, Paimon. Hello, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the crown ready?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yes, we're just waiting for Zuria now. She hasn't arrived yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's wait for her a little while! Or actually, maybe we can go find her? It's not too far from here, anyway. Didn't she say she just lives on the hill over there?
#Hey, {NICKNAME}! Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, and speaking of...

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: Found you two at long last... I'm so glad that you're both all right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you here, Miss Delaroche? And what could have happened to us?

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: What could have happened? That Water Imp Thelxie, of course! After I gave you that commission the other day, I began to get worried and went asking about the boy that went missing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that? We've got that all figured out now! The boy you heard about was just Freminet. Even the missing fish was his fault. Don't worry, we'll help you get the fish back as soon as we're done with this job!

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Sorry about that, I've been diving in the area recently...

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: Huh? Freminet? Diving? No no no... that's not what happened at all. I've heard a completely different account...

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: What I was told is that about a month ago, a child tied a bunch of heavy seashells onto his body and walked into this open stretch of water. He never came back... what could that be, if not that Water Imp's work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are... Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: One hundred percent sure! I've confirmed the account with several veteran fishermen I know. The child was only eight years old... His name was Lescot. Lescot Destree.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Wait... Lescot Destree?

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's the name! They say the family took on the name after moving to the city from a place called Destree. Anyway, his mother is a pretty famous art dealer, while his father passed away from an accident many years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: *sigh* Naturally, his mother was devastated by the incident, and fell terribly ill. It's said that she left the Court of Fontaine, and no one knows where she has gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It can't be... right? Lescot Destree... Zuria Destree... It must be some sort of a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like we need to pay a visit to the Destree house.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Miss! We've got to go check on something right now!

dialogues.speaker: Delaroche
dialogues.text: Oh, I see... Well, you go on ahead. I just came to make sure that you're both all right. I'll head back then... Please remember to take care!

talks.objective: Go to Madame Zuria Destree's house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excuse us! Is anyone here? Is this Madame Destree's place?

dialogues.speaker: A male voice from inside the room
dialogues.text: Who are you? I have a patient here who needs quiet bed rest. Please leave us be unless you have anything urgent to report.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who is the patient?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The door opens after a brief moment of silence. A man walks out with a confused look in his eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: This is the residence of Zuria Destree, and I am Jalacan, her family doctor. What did you mean by your question just now? Who else could be my patient?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your patient should be... Zuria's son, right? She told us herself that her son had contracted Loneliness Syndrome...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: No, you're right, young master Lescot did have that illness once upon a time, but he's... Well, the young master's no longer with us, and now, the Madame has come down with the same illness. Are you... her friends by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You inform the doctor of all that's happened in the past few days between some breaks of silence...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: Ah... So when she had requested time to go out over the past few days, it was so she could spend them with you.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: So, if I'm understanding this right... The one who's suffering from uncontrollable delusions is the Madame herself? She believes her son is still alive?

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: That is correct. When the young master... disappeared, she was organizing an art exhibit that she had specifically prepared for him. But since she had to leave the house, she was unable to see her son one last time...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: That might have been the trigger for her regret, or perhaps the family's fall into loneliness and grief was inevitable as soon as the old master passed away. First the son, and then the mother...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how could that be... She really looked like she had a handle on everything. Her smile was so lovely, and she even told us to stay optimistic. But you're saying, she...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: Those actions are proof that she can no longer differentiate between fantasy and reality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then... all the other things that she told us about her son... Were those fake, too?

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: No, those were all real, although they were all things that happened before the young master left us for good. Madame's time has just never moved forward since his passing.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I see, so after her son left, she created a fantasy world where her son was still with her. She was looking for a way to cure his illness when she ran into us...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, how is Zuria now?

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: She has been in a good mood the past few days, even humming a song when she returned from her stroll. She even began discussing with me the idea of using deliberate guidance to ease the illness. It was all going well, until last night...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: ...She spent a whole night staring at the shell the young master left behind, and the words that he had inscribed onto it... Then, she broke down once more. I prescribed some sedatives, and she's currently resting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... But then what should we do? How can we help her? There has to be something we can do...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Don't panic, Paimon... Even though this is a devastating piece of news, we must all calm down first...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (What should we do? I need to think... I need to remember the old House of the Hearth, and the children who lived in it... Those patients, and what their doctors said then... Ah! What if...)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Dr. Jalacan, have you seen a picture book? The Madame should have brought it back with her.

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: Hmm... Are you thinking about trying the guidance therapy she talked to me about before? ...It's worth a shot. I'll go get the book.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The doctor quickly retrieves the book and hands it to Freminet.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yes... This is it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We still need to finish the adventure and the picture book?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: That's right. If what Dr. Jalacan said was true, the past few days have been very helpful to Zuria. So we should complete this journey.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: We need to show her that her child has found a happy ending in the world of her dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... But wouldn't that just make it harder for her to accept reality?

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: One must first face reality before accepting it. The Madame has been crushed by her feelings of grief, and can no longer bring herself to face reality. Our first priority would be to get her out of this state.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Right... Before today, I had thought she wanted to use Thelxie's Fantastic Adventures to save her son. But now, I think she might need it to save herself.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: And if we could complete it, we should be able to give her some feeling of inspiration and closure. Maybe those feelings would be enough to give her some courage to face reality again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll have to give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: There's no time to waste... Let's set off right away.

talks.objective: Go to the Kingdom of Water Imps

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here again... This is the final part of Thelxie's journey, but the most important person is missing...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Everyone... Please don't be so down and gloomy. Remember what she told us? If we were to feel troubled, the patient would become anxious as well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, you're right, Paimon needs to smile! If we have to give something to Zuria, it should be our smiles! We have to keep smiling as we finish this adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then she'll be able to recover, right everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm sure she will.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm sure she will.

talks.objective: Leave the Kingdom of Water Imps

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I have to go. I made a promise to my friends, and I'm already very late...

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: But Madame, you're still...

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Don't try to stop me! Today's the most important day for treating Thelxie! We'll use the guidance method. Didn't you also say that you think it'd work?

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: I'm not trying to stop you, Madame. It's just... Could you tell me the name of your child?

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Dr. Jalacan, how can you forget the name of your own patient? His name is Thelxie! He's the prince of the Kingdom of Water Imps! We will go today to reclaim his crown, and attend his coronation ceremony!

dialogues.speaker: Jalacan
dialogues.text: I see... Madame... Please rest assured, everything is still on schedule, your friends have already departed to find... Wait... Look! They've already returned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zuria, Zuria! We've retrieved the crown!

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon... Everyone... Have you, really?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yes, but the coronation ceremony still hasn't taken place, because we felt like you should be the one to preside over it...

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Wonderful, how wonderful! Thelxie... my child... My child, are you hearing this? Everything you lost will now come back to you, and soon, very soon, you will never be lonely again...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: And the last page of the picture book... It's still waiting for you to illustrate and color.

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Right, the picture book, the picture book. But I don't know what I should put on the last page...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Thelxie and his friends all know what should go on it! Get ready, Zuria, we'll describe everything for you!

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Okay... okay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem... At last, Thelxie and his friends were able to drive off the final invading monsters and achieve a dashing victory. Their success was complete, and the recovered crown resplendent.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: The Water Imps, finally returning to their homes, showered the prince with love and applause as he greeted them. They once again offered their precious shells to the prince, and reconstructed the rainbow bridge of old. As he watched the scene unfold, the Prince could not help but be touched by its beauty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Moved by everyone's happiness, the Prince stepped onto the rainbow bridge and took a good look at all the friends who had gone on the journey with him. There stood {NICKNAME}, Goddess Paimon, Freminet, and...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where's the last person? The prince looked frantically around, but could not find the person he wanted to see most. At that moment, the person suddenly appeared on the other side of the bridge. She walked towards him with a smile and slowly lifted her veil.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: The prince could not hold back his tears. He recognized, then, that the mysterious person that had been by his side the whole time was none other than his mother.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Zuria walked across the bridge and placed the crown above the prince's head. She smiled down upon him as she said, "My prince — my king — you shall never, ever need to feel lonely again."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the end of the story, Zuria.

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Thank you... Thank you all...

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: I am so sorry, my child, Maman should have spent more time with you... Did you hear the story? You'll never have to feel lonely again...

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Mhm! Maman loves you, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's happening? Is Zuria talking to Thelxie?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is Thelxie saying?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Quick, put on my diving helmet! There's a transcription module in it that's compatible with Thelxie's output signals. You should be able to use it to understand what Thelxie's saying...

dialogues.speaker: Thelxie
dialogues.text: I love you, Maman!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So that's what Thelxie is saying...

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Maman... Maman loves you, too...

dialogues.speaker: Lescot Destree
dialogues.text: But I love you more, Maman!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, what is this?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: What? Did you see something?

dialogues.speaker: Lescot Destree
dialogues.text: Maman, I'm getting a little sleepy... If it's time for bed, can you hum a lullaby to me again?

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Of course, my dearest child... As long as you want to hear it, Maman will always hum for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lescot Destree
dialogues.text: Thank you, Maman! Your lullaby has always been my favorite. Now that I've heard it, I can return to my dream, and to the Kingdom of Water Imps in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Zuria Destree
dialogues.text: Ah, my poor darling... Please don't forget, I will always love you. My love is... greater than the entire distance between here and the Kingdom of Water Imps.

dialogues.speaker: Lescot Destree
dialogues.text: I won't forget, Maman... And so is my love for you. Greater than the entire distance between here and the Kingdom of Water Imps.

dialogues.speaker: Lescot Destree
dialogues.text: Goodnight, Maman!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Three days later, at Freminet's camp...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Freminet! Why did you call us in such a hurry? Did you hear something from Zuria? Ohh, if it's not good news, Paimon doesn't want to hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it's definitely great news. The Madame came here for a visit just now with her doctor. Color has returned to her cheeks, and she sounded full of energy as well.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: She said she'd like to return to the Court to continue hosting the art exhibit, but this time, she'll work with her doctor to exhibit some picture books related to the illness.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Of course, Thelxie's Fantastic Adventures and the guidance therapy will be included in the exhibit as well. She'd like to use her experience to help others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's wonderful! Whew, so it wasn't bad news after all.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Mhm. Here, please take this picture book with you. The Madame wanted you to have it. If, at some point in the future, you were to run into someone with similar troubles, she hopes the book would be of use to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But this is her son's story, right? Is it really okay to give the book to us?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it's just a copy. She still has the original. It's extremely important to her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, then there's no problem! Ahh, it feels good knowing we've contributed to something important. Paimon definitely didn't expect the fantasy adventure to be so useful... Paimon was a little worried about how everything would turn out. After all, fantasy is just fantasy.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Paimon, do you know what the Madame said?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: She said... that at the moment when she placed the crown on Thelxie's head, she felt like she really saw something beautiful. Her child had returned, and he told her that he loved her.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: She also said that was when she was finally able to bid farewell to her son. She felt like at that moment, she was healed by some mystical power, and she was filled with courage from head to toe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh!? Really? But could that just be another part of her fantasy?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Perhaps, but if fantasy is just fantasy, and the fantasy world is not real, then how could it still grant us these powers that we can continue to use in the real world?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... perhaps fantasy is not just fantasy after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—But what else could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: A descent of the fairytale world into the real world. At that time, the wondrous fairytale temporarily became reality, and influenced real things in our world. That has to be what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: You saw it too, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But that can't be what happened, right? There's just no way! Wouldn't it be like a miracle if that really happened?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yes... I suppose that would be a miracle.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I hope that everyone who's found themselves in a dark place would be able to see something beautiful, and experience a miracle for themselves.
